items.title: citation-rule-check.mjs blames the doc even when README is the side that moved
items.acceptance: When README.md`s citation-selection sentence is reworded while the history doc`s quote block is left untouched, tools/citation-rule-check.mjs`s failure message identifies README.md as the document that moved, rather than reporting that the history doc has diverged. The existing doc-side perturbation must still name the history doc, and the honest-text converse control must still exit 0. Both directions demonstrated by real runs against a scratch copy.
items.notes: Found by the cycle-2 conductor gate, BEYOND the W-3 acceptance clause (which scopes failability to perturbing the QUOTE, and that case attributes correctly). Measured: perturbing README`s sentence -- `the push that carried the last change to` -> `the push that carried the change to` -- while leaving the doc alone still prints `FAIL: docs/node-support-citation-history.md has diverged`. Every factual clause in that message is true (the block is genuinely not a substring of README any more) but the direction of attribution is wrong. The builder`s own Run D showed a README-side message, but only for a MISSING HEADING -- a structurally different failure, not a body divergence. A substring check cannot infer direction from two files alone; closing this likely needs a third anchor (e.g. the committed blob of README at the last green commit) or a message that names the pair without asserting which side moved. Not a gate failure for W-3; a real defect on the record.
items.verify_note: All three acceptance directions verified independently. items.title: citation-rule-check.mjs can compare against an ANCESTOR repo HEAD without noticing
items.acceptance: When tools/citation-rule-check.mjs runs in a directory that is NOT itself a git repository but is nested inside an unrelated one, it must not state that it compared a file against "its own git HEAD version". Either it verifies that the resolved git toplevel is the directory under check and otherwise takes the undetermined-direction path, or its message stops asserting whose HEAD it used. The three existing directions (README-side, doc-side, honest control) must all still behave as they do today, demonstrated by real runs.
items.notes: Found by the cycle-3 conductor gate, BEYOND the P-1 acceptance clause. Measured: git rev-parse --show-toplevel from a nested checkout with .git deleted returns /opt/targets/aphorism-cli (the PARENT repo), so `git show HEAD:README.md` silently resolves against an ancestor. In the gate the ancestor happened to be the same project, so the attribution looked correct - that coincidence is exactly what makes it worth fixing. Run genuinely outside any repo the fallback DOES fire correctly (verified), so this is narrow: only the nested-inside-unrelated-repo case. Low severity; the failure mode is a confidently-stated attribution that could name the wrong side. [CYCLE 6 DONE] Builder added resolvedToplevelIsOwnRoot(): `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from rootDir, realpath-compared to rootDir; readHeadBlob() returns null when they differ, routing to the pre-existing honest undetermined-direction message. Conductor gate: C8' rebuilt the nested-non-repo scenario independently, confirmed `--show-toplevel` still resolves to the ANCESTOR /opt/targets/aphorism-cli, and showed the tool no longer asserts 'own git HEAD version' and instead takes the undetermined path. C9' is the converse control in a clone that IS its own toplevel: the tool still names README as the side that moved AND still names the git anchor, so the fix is narrow rather than a blanket degrade. C10 is the honest control on the live tree (exit 0, OK). NOTE: the first-pass cells C8/C9 FAILED because the conductor's perturbation rewrote the '### Node support' HEADING, which the tool matches exactly, short-circuiting at the no-section branch before any attribution ran - a gate defect, not a defect in this work. See D-R8-17.

items.title: tools/mutation-matrix.mjs cannot measure any tree but 20b7ede, so W-8 is unsatisfiable as shipped
items.acceptance:
tools/mutation-matrix.mjs can measure a caller-named tree.
A. Invoked with NO arguments it still measures 20b7ede and its emitted matrix is
   verdict-for-verdict identical to tools/mutation-matrix-baseline.json. The default
   path is a frozen contract: tools/run-all.mjs invokes it with zero cliArgs, and the
   committed baseline JSON is the comparison W-8 depends on.
B. Invoked so as to name a different tree, it demonstrably measures THAT tree — the run
   must state the resolved full sha of what it measured, and that sha must equal the
   named rev resolved independently.
C. A mutation whose transcribed guardTitle no longer exists in the measured tree must
   NOT abort the run. W-7 consolidated two same-row guards into one, so this case is
   live at HEAD, not hypothetical. The CAUGHT/SILENT verdict is what S-1 turns on;
   attribution to a named guard is secondary and must degrade to an explicitly recorded
   state rather than throwing.
items.notes: Line 89 as shipped: const BASELINE = '20b7ede', with a detached checkout at it near line 482. D-R8-12: as shipped, W-8 "re-run the matrix at final HEAD" would measure the baseline TWICE and return a guaranteed-identical matrix — which W-8's own clause anticipates as a legitimate null result. The two outcomes are observationally identical, so a builder could discharge W-8 honestly and be wrong. Do not change WHAT the mutation set is; only what tree it is measured against.

items.title: mutation-matrix.mjs can emit machine-readable JSON only for the default rev, so W-8 has no structured side to compare at HEAD
items.acceptance: A matrix run against a non-default rev can produce the same structured record the default run writes, WITHOUT being able to overwrite tools/mutation-matrix-baseline.json. The existing refusal of `--rev` together with `--write-baseline` must stay in force — that guard is correct and is not what this item relaxes; the committed baseline must remain writable only from the default rev. Proof: a HEAD run emits a record that can be diffed row-by-row against the committed baseline by a caller, and the committed baseline file is byte-unmoved by that run.
items.notes: Found by the cycle-5 gate, not by the builder. W-8 must prove "no mutation detected at baseline goes undetected at final HEAD". At HEAD the tool prints that verdict only as TEXT: --write-baseline is refused whenever --rev is given (correctly, since it would corrupt the instrument), and there is no other structured output path. So W-8 would have to compare a committed JSON against scraped prose — precisely the "never assert against prose matched by regex" failure the playbook warns about. The cycle-5 gate hit this directly: it could compare the DEFAULT run verdict-for-verdict against the JSON, but had to fall back to tool-owned text lines for the HEAD run. [CYCLE 6 DONE] Builder added a `--json` flag that routes the human report to stderr and prints the SAME `baseline` record --write-baseline persists, to stdout. Conductor gate: C3 proved the zero-arg contract byte-identical to the pre-change HEAD tool (both run, stdout diffed); C4 parsed the ENTIRE --rev HEAD --json stdout as one JSON document and diffed it row-by-row by id against the committed baseline (18 committed rows, 15 at HEAD, 15 shared, 0 verdict differences, M01-M03 listed explicitly as baseline-only rather than folded into a pass); C5 is the converse control (zero-arg stdout does NOT parse as JSON, so the flag is not a no-op); C6 showed --rev+--write-baseline still refused with exit 2, and also refused with --json added, so --json is not a back door to the committed file; C7 showed the baseline sha256 unmoved across every run. C2' confirmed structurally that `baseline` is declared at top level (L774) before both the write branch (L791) and the emit block (L804), so --json cannot be a latent ReferenceError.

items.title: REPORT.md's commit-count claim prints a git range that selects one fewer commit than the number beside it
items.acceptance: REPORT.md's closing line states a commit count whose printed git range actually selects that count, verified by running the printed range. Either the range becomes `912a2a4^..d899fe0` (which returns 13) or prose that does not read as a git range, or the number becomes 12 with the existing `912a2a4..d899fe0`. The commit list must still include cycle 0's KICKOFF commit in whatever framing is chosen, since it is one of the run's own commits. No other line of REPORT.md changes.
items.notes: Found by the cycle-8 conductor gate (C13), BEYOND W-10's acceptance clause, which carries no commit-count requirement at all. Measured in .swarm/runs/cycle-008-verify-W-10-c13-addendum.txt: REPORT.md says "(13 commits, `912a2a4`..`d899fe0`)"; `git rev-list --count 912a2a4..d899fe0` = 12 because git's A..B EXCLUDES A, while `912a2a4^..d899fe0` = 13. 912a2a4 IS run #8's cycle-0 KICKOFF commit (its parent 20b7ede is run #7's wrap-up and this run's baseline), so the NUMBER 13 is true of the run's own commits and only the NOTATION beside it is wrong by one. A reader who runs the printed range gets 12 and concludes the report is off by one — which is exactly the kind of self-inflicted accuracy defect a report about measurement discipline cannot afford. Same ruling shape as D-R8-7 and D-R8-8: recorded as a new item, not rounded into a FAIL of the work and not buried. See D-R8-21.

items.title: The identity control is self-certifying: only its verdict STRING is read, never the suite totals printed beside it
items.acceptance: The identity control's GREEN ruling must be a function of the recorded measurement -- at minimum suite.fail === 0 and suite.skipped === 0, and identity.gitDependentGuards.ran must actually be consulted. A record whose identity recorded failing tests must turn the run red. Converse control: an honest GREEN record still passes.
items.notes: REPRODUCED on the committed artifact via the default path, and confirmed structurally by the conductor's own reading. detection-floor.mjs:388 is `if (!idn || idn.verdict !== 'GREEN')` -- the suite totals are interpolated into the DISPLAY line at :386-387 and never compared. The tool printed 'GREEN (128 tests, 121 pass, 7 fail, 0 skipped)' and then, later, 'identity control GREEN on both sides', exit 0 -- it prints the contradiction itself and rules green anyway. Conductor discriminator: `grep -c gitDependentGuards` = 1 in the final record, 0 in detection-floor.mjs, so that field cannot be consulted on ANY path, not merely the default one. This is the control that makes every CAUGHT verdict meaningful.

items.title: An internally impossible row (CAUGHT with a fully green suite and no fired guards) is bucketed SAME-GUARD

An internally inconsistent row must turn the run red rather than be printed as 'still detected, target guard fired on both sides'.
items.notes: REPRODUCED on the committed artifact via the default path. A row with verdict 'CAUGHT', caughtByTargetGuard true, suite {tests:128, pass:128, fail:0, skipped:0} and firedGuards [] was bucketed SAME-GUARD and printed as target-guard-fired, exit 0. Conductor read the path directly: :447-449 tests only the verdict string and the boolean; firedGuards is used solely to build the display list in the guardChanged branch. No cross-field consistency check exists anywhere in the reader.

items.title: A CAUGHT verdict counts ANY failing test, so M07's detection is structurally guaranteed and its floor row is unfalsifiable
items.acceptance: A CAUGHT verdict must be attributable to a guard that fires BECAUSE the claim became false -- not to a guard that fires because the working tree is dirty. Environmental failures (the base-to-working-tree citation guard, which asserts on any uncommitted src/ edit) must be excluded from the CAUGHT determination or recorded separately. Proof required: M07 must be capable of reporting SILENT when its semantic guards are absent.
items.notes: REPRODUCED both halves. mutation-matrix.mjs:709 is `verdict = run.totals.fail > 0 ? 'CAUGHT' : 'SILENT'`. M07 is the sole 'derivation-source' mutation (edits src/corpus.js, :302-310), and test/node-support-citation.test.js's base-to-working-tree guard ASSERTS (does not skip) on any uncommitted src/ diff whenever the base resolves in a full non-shallow clone -- which the matrix's own scratch clone guarantees, and which the identity control HARD-REQUIRES to run un-skipped. With every semantic guard for M07's claim deleted, the suite still failed exactly 1 test (the citation guard), so the verdict would still read CAUGHT. NUANCE the reviewer understated and the verifier corrected: at real HEAD two genuine semantic guards also fire on M07, so today's CAUGHT is not wholly environmental -- the defect is that the verdict rule cannot DISTINGUISH them, so the row can never go red even after all semantic coverage is gone. [CYCLE 11 NOTE, planning] RV-5 edits tools/mutation-matrix.mjs, which is inside detection-floor's VERDICT_RELEVANT set. Landing it therefore re-stales tools/mutation-matrix-final.json exactly as cycle 10 did (see W-15). Budget a ~100s re-measure in the SAME cycle that lands RV-5, or the next cycle opens on a STALE instrument again. [CYCLE 14 VERIFIED] Verified by /opt/swarm/runs/gate-c14-rv5.mjs, 5/5 cells. B2 is the cell the acceptance clause demanded: on a GREEN induced tree at a222eab with M07's three MEASURED semantic guards deleted, PRE-fix reports CAUGHT off a single environmental fire and POST-fix reports SILENT, while still recording that the environmental guard fired (B5). B4: all 18 verdicts at real HEAD unchanged. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-014-verify-RV-5.txt.

Either the FRESH-BY-CONTENT exemption cross-checks the record, or --remeasure performs its reproduction cross-check when the record is an ancestor whose verdict-relevant tree is byte-identical. Today's gate is inverted -- it cross-checks only when the record is already at HEAD, the case needing it least.

items.title: The count-floor detector is one-directionally evadable, so 'VERDICT: ABSENT' is weaker than the categorical sentence it prints
items.acceptance: The detectors must catch a real suite-size floor written in ordinary forms -- at minimum both operand orders (`n > 120` AND `120 < n`) and a directory census that does not spell 'test' inside the readdirSync call. Or section G must stop printing a categorical negative and state what it actually searched for. Proof: a genuinely working, genuinely failable floor guard must be detected, and the clean tree must still report ABSENT.
items.notes: REPRODUCED including the one-directionality, which is the decisive part. The verifier's evading guard genuinely runs, genuinely passes at the true count, and genuinely FAILS when the floor exceeds the count (raised to 900: 'AssertionError: suite shrank below the floor of 900') -- it is a working floor, not a prop. Written `120 < n` with readdirSync(dir): F.i NONE, F.ii NONE, 'VERDICT: ABSENT. No guard anywhere in test/ (or CI) asserts any floor' -- while section E lists that very guard by title. Written `n > 120`: F.i fires, verdict flips to PRESENT. Converse control holds: on the clean tree ABSENT is currently TRUE. So the published verdict is not wrong today -- but this run RETIRED count-floors on the strength of it, and it is an evadable detector presented as a settled negative. Compounds RV-1: detection-floor's W8-R1 text defers the reworded-claim case to exactly this tool. [CYCLE 11 DONE] Builder took BOTH routes the clause allows: widened the probes (F.i.b literal-on-the-left, F.i.c same-file named const, F.ii.b directory enumeration matched by CALLEE only) and replaced section G's categorical negative with a verdict BOUNDED BY THE SEARCH, printing the probe list from the same FLOOR_PROBES table the scan iterates. Conductor gate planted its OWN failable floor guard (readdirSync(HERE), literal-on-the-left comparison) in an isolated clone carrying the builder's worktree file proven equal by sha: PRE-FIX tool F.i NONE / F.ii NONE / VERDICT ABSENT; POST-FIX same tree F.i.b + F.ii.b fire / VERDICT PRESENT. Guard proven real: PASSES at floor 120, FAILS at 900 with 'suite shrank below the floor of 900'. Converse control with the guard removed: ABSENT, no false positive. Sections A-E byte-identical old vs new (31572 bytes both).

items.title: The headline recommendation presents a tautology of the tool's own definitions as a measured finding, with a dead else-branch
items.acceptance: Either make gap 0 structurally reachable (so the counter measures something), or relabel the finding as the definitional identity it is and drop the causal attribution to CI/push semantics. The unreachable else-branch must go or become reachable. The conclusion may well be TRUE in the world -- the requirement is that the tool stop presenting it as measured when it is entailed by its own data structures.
items.notes: REPRODUCED BY THE CONDUCTOR by reading the code, not taken on the reviewer's word. `verdict` is single-valued per commit (:391); `breaks` = commits with verdict 'RED' (:441); the repair scan (:484-494) starts at i = b.idx but accepts only `st.verdict === 'green'`, so it can never select the breaking commit itself. Therefore gap >= 1 always, `selfRepairs` (:517) is identically 0 for every possible input, `allGapPositive` (:660) is identically true whenever gaps.length > 0, and the else-branch at :671-673 ('the two-commit shape is convention here, not a consequence of the claim') is unreachable dead code. The report nonetheless prints 'THE GAP IS NEVER ZERO, AND CANNOT BE ... That is arithmetic, not indiscipline: the citation names a CI RUN ID' -- attributing to CI semantics a 0 that its own definitions guarantee. In a run whose whole thesis is measurement-not-prose, a tautology printed as a finding is the defect. [CYCLE 16 VERIFIED] see .swarm/runs/run8-cycle-016-verify-RV-13.txt; gate sealed by hash before dispatch (bfc438c1f998695f8965...).
